utfall: kunnskapsgrunnlag: én RCT og 12 registerstudier, hovedsakelig muskel/skjelett eller psykiske lidelser; ingen sikre konklusjoner om effekt
sitat: Forskningsgrunnlaget for effekten av gradert sykmelding sammenlignet med full syk‐ melding består av én RCT og 12 RBer, med totalt ca 2,74 millioner personer som er syk‐ meldt på grunn av hovedsakelig muskel‐ og skjelettplager eller mentale lidelser.

utfall: ingen effektestimat; mindre belegg for gradert sykmelding ved vanlige psykiske lidelser enn ved fysiske plager
sitat: activation in general, and PTSL in particular, often concentrate on workers with physical (e.g., musculoskeletal) complaints, suggesting that there is less evidence in regard to the effectiveness of PTSL targeted at other salient diagnoses such as common mental disorders

utfall: full gjenvunnet arbeidsevne, psykiske lidelser, gradert etter 60 dager med full (gjennomsnittlig behandlingseffekt)
sammenligning: gradert sykmelding etter 60 dager med full vs. full
sitat: the average treatment effect of PTSL is relatively low (0.015) when assigned in the beginning of the spell, but relatively high (0.387), and statistically significant, when assigned after 60 days of FTSL.

utfall: full gjenvunnet arbeidsevne, psykiske lidelser, gradert fra start (gjennomsnittlig behandlingseffekt, ikke signifikant)

sitat: the average treatment effect of PTSL is relatively low (0.015) when assigned in the beginning of the spell, but relatively high (0.387), and statistically significant, when assigned after 60 days of FTSL.

utfall: tid til ordinær arbeidstid, psykiske lidelser: ingen effekt når det kontrolleres for uobserverte forskjeller (bare sammendrag)
sammenligning: gradert vs. full sykmelding, kontroll for uobserverte forskjeller
sitat: Our analyses show that PTSL has no effect on the duration until returning to regular working hours for employees with mental disorders.

utfall: varig retur til arbeid (minst 28 dager), psykiske og muskel/skjelett samlet
sammenligning: gradert vs. full sykmelding de første 12 ukene, matchet
sitat: A higher proportion showed sustained RTW after part- compared to full-time sick leave [absolute risk difference 8.0%, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) 5.3–10.9].

utfall: varig retur etter diagnose: forskjell ved psykiske lidelser, ingen ved muskel/skjelett (tallet per diagnose er ikke lesbart i tabellen)
sammenligning: gradert vs. full sykmelding de første 12 ukene, matchet
sitat: A difference in favor of the part-time sick leave group was seen in both genders, all age groups – particularly in those aged 45–64 years – and for mental disorders, whereas there was no difference in those with musculoskeletal disease.

utfall: arbeidsdeltakelse (andel av året i arbeid), psykiske lidelser, forskjell-i-forskjell
sammenligning: gradert vs. full sykmelding etter lovendringen 2007
sitat: A statistically significantly larger effect (12.8%, 95% CI 9.0% to 16.5%) was found in mental disorders as compared with the other diagnostic categories.

sammenligning: gradert vs. full sykmelding etter lovendringen 2007
sitat: the decline was 5% (absolute difference-in-differences) smaller in the intervention than in the comparison group

sitat: Partial sickness benefit reduced the risk (change in absolute risk) of full disability pension by 6% and increased the risk of partial disability pension by 8% compared with full sick leave. The effects did not differ markedly for the two main diagnostic groups of musculoskeletal and mental disorders.

sitat: For individuals with problems related to mental health we find no significant effects of graded return-to-work. Moreover, and contrary to the overall findings, for these individuals starting the graded return-to-work trajectory one week earlier decreases the probability to return to work within two years with 3 percentage point.

utfall: ordinært arbeid og selvforsørgelse: effekt av gradert tilbakeføring bare ved fysiske (ikke psykiske) lidelser; ingen eget tall for psykiske lidelser i teksten

sitat: These programs are associated with strong and long-lasting eﬀects, but only for workers sick-listed from regular employment and for those with physical (non-mental) disorders.

sitat: At follow-up, 88% of the GRTW group had returned to work compared to only 73% of the controls (RR = 1.22, 1.13–1.31).
